findings.title: NoSuchElementException if no recovery credential exists
findings.body: The constructor calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking `isPresent()`. If `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns an empty Optional (e.g., the user has no recovery codes credential in either federated or local storage), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` at runtime. The new `getCredential` method has a more complex lookup path (federated first, then local) which increases the chance of returning empty compared to the previous direct local lookup. A guard or explicit exception with a meaningful message should be added.

findings.title: removeStoredCredentialById may not remove federated credentials
findings.body: When all recovery codes are consumed, `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` is called. However, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` now returns credentials from federated storage first. If the credential originates from a federated/user storage provider, `removeStoredCredentialById` targets the local credential store and may silently fail to remove the credential from the external storage. This leaves a stale credential with all codes consumed. On subsequent logins, the authenticator's `configuredFor` check may still see the credential as present, but validation will fail since all codes are used, potentially confusing the user or causing unexpected behavior until the required action to regenerate codes is completed.

findings.title: NullPointerException in getCredentials if user not found in map
findings.body: In `getCredentials(RealmModel realm, UserModel user)`, `getMyUser(user)` can return null if the user is not present in the `users` map. The subsequent access to `myUser.recoveryCodes` on line 235 will throw a NullPointerException. A null check on `myUser` should be added before accessing its fields, returning an empty stream if the user is not found.

findings.title: updateCredential may return false for reasons other than unsupported type
findings.body: The method `createRecoveryCodesCredential` interprets `updateCredential` returning `false` as 'user storage does not support this credential type' and falls back to local storage. However, `updateCredential` on a user storage provider may return `false` for other reasons (e.g., validation failure, transient error). In such cases, the code silently creates the credential locally instead of propagating the error, which could lead to inconsistent state where the user storage rejected the update for a valid reason but the credential is still created locally. The existing `createOTPCredential` method has the same pattern, but it's worth documenting or handling this distinction.

findings.title: No test for fallback to local storage when user storage does not support recovery codes
findings.body: The test only covers the scenario where the user storage supports recovery codes (the `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` was modified to support them). There is no test verifying that when a user storage provider does NOT support recovery codes (i.e., `updateCredential` returns false or `supportsCredentialType` returns false), the credential is correctly created in the local Keycloak database. This is the core fallback behavior introduced by this PR and should be tested.
